messages.subject: Future models and how to classify a good distribution model?
parts:
Good morning, thank you for accepting me in the group. I have some doubts regarding the parameters that should be used in wallace's results to choose a model. In this case I am working with the potential distribution of a species of the Procyon family and when obtaining the data we do not know which variables are the corresponding ones for the choice of the model. messages.author: 881c0dd9c7b0d196
messages.subject: Re: Future models and how to classify a good distribution model?
parts:
Hello,
To answer your first question, there is no "right" answer. Wallace offers several methods to evaluate model performance (as seen in your screenshot; area under the curve (AUC), continuous boyce index (CBI), omission rate (OR), AICc). One method is not better compared to another, you might even find one model performing well in one method and poorly with another. You can find information on the specifics of these methods in the Model component guidance text. Here you'll find info on each method and what values are optimal. Furthermore, you can also try several models and compare the predictions in regards to ecological realism- is one predicting areas you know the species is not known to be found? You mentioned the variables- you can find the variable response curves in the Response Curve module of the Visualize component.

As for the GCMs, WorldClim offers a variety of GCMs (General Circulation Models/Global Climate Models) at four different RCPs (Representative Concentration Pathways) that Wallace uses for future projections. Information on the different models can be found here https://worldclim.org/cmip6maps.html or https://www.worldclim.org/data/cmip6/cmip6climate.html. Please note, the usage of RCPs was recently replaced with Shared Socio-economic Pathways (SSPs), so you may see that in the literature instead. 

I hope that information helps.
Bethany Johnson
